1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	MVP Validation: Confounding DAG with K=3 Multiclass Annotation Error
4	
5	Verifies that multiclass (K>=3) annotation error in causal inference
6	produces qualitatively different bias patterns than binary misclassification.
7	
8	DAG: A -> T, A -> Y, T -> Y
9	  A in {0,1,2}: true 3-class confounder
10	  A*: noisy annotation via 3x3 confusion matrix C
11	  T: continuous treatment
12	  Y: continuous outcome
13	
14	DGP:
15	  T = alpha_1*1[A=1] + alpha_2*1[A=2] + eta,  eta ~ N(0, sigma_T^2)
16	  Y = beta_T*T + beta_1*1[A=1] + beta_2*1[A=2] + eps,  eps ~ N(0, sigma_Y^2)
17	  P(A*=j|A=i) = C[j,i]  (C is column-stochastic)
18	
19	Key result: plim gamma_hat = (E[Z'Z])^{-1} E[Z'X] beta
20	  where Z uses A* dummies, X uses true A dummies.
21	
22	Pass criteria:
23	  1. Theory vs MC 95% CI match: 5/5
24	  2. >=1 non-differential C produces away-from-null bias
25	  3. Binary collapse bias != multiclass theory prediction
26	
27	Dependencies: numpy, scipy (standard library only)
28	"""
29	
30	import numpy as np
31	from scipy import stats
32	import time
33	
34	# ============================================================
35	# Configuration
36	# ============================================================
37	N_SAMPLES = 10_000
38	M_REPS = 1_000
39	SEED = 42
40	
41	P_A = np.array([0.4, 0.35, 0.25])
42	ALPHA = np.array([1.5, -1.0])        # alpha_1, alpha_2
43	BETA_T = 2.0                          # true causal effect
44	BETA_A = np.array([1.0, -0.5])       # beta_1, beta_2
45	SIGMA_T = 1.0
46	SIGMA_Y = 1.0
47	
48	
49	# ============================================================
50	# Confusion matrix definitions
51	# ============================================================
52	def make_confusion_matrices():
53	    """5 confusion matrix structures. Each column sums to 1."""
54	    matrices = {}
55	
56	    # 1. Symmetric high accuracy: diag=0.8, off-diag=0.1
57	    matrices["1_sym_high"] = (np.array([
58	        [0.80, 0.10, 0.10],
59	        [0.10, 0.80, 0.10],
60	        [0.10, 0.10, 0.80]
61	    ]), False)
62	
63	    # 2. Asymmetric: P(A*=1|A=0)=0.30 >> P(A*=0|A=1)=0.05
64	    matrices["2_asymmetric"] = (np.array([
65	        [0.65, 0.05, 0.10],
66	        [0.30, 0.85, 0.10],
67	        [0.05, 0.10, 0.80]
68	    ]), False)
69	
70	    # 3. Structural: classes 1<->2 heavily confused, class 0 clean
71	    matrices["3_struct_12"] = (np.array([
72	        [0.90, 0.05, 0.05],
73	        [0.05, 0.65, 0.30],
74	        [0.05, 0.30, 0.65]
75	    ]), False)
76	
77	    # 4. Near-random: diag~0.4
78	    matrices["4_near_rand"] = (np.array([
79	        [0.40, 0.30, 0.30],
80	        [0.30, 0.40, 0.30],
81	        [0.30, 0.30, 0.40]
82	    ]), False)
83	
84	    # 5. Differential: base C + T-dependent error increase
85	    matrices["5_differen"] = (np.array([
86	        [0.80, 0.10, 0.10],
87	        [0.10, 0.80, 0.10],
88	        [0.10, 0.10, 0.80]
89	    ]), True)
90	
91	    for name, (C, _) in matrices.items():
92	        assert np.allclose(C.sum(axis=0), 1.0), f"{name}: columns don't sum to 1"
93	        assert (C >= 0).all(), f"{name}: negative entries"
94	
95	    return matrices
96	
97	
98	# ============================================================
99	# Theoretical bias (exact, for non-differential C)
100	# ============================================================
101	def theoretical_bias_exact(C, p_A, alpha, beta_T, beta_A, sigma_T):
102	    """
103	    Compute plim of OLS with misclassified A* dummies.
104	
105	    plim gamma = (E[Z'Z])^{-1} E[Z'X] beta
106	    Z = (1, T, D*_1, D*_2),  X = (1, T, D_1, D_2)
107	
108	    Returns: (bias_on_betaT, full_plim_vector)
109	    """
110	    p0, p1, p2 = p_A
111	    a1, a2 = alpha
112	    b1, b2 = beta_A
113	    beta = np.array([0.0, beta_T, b1, b2])
114	
115	    ET = a1 * p1 + a2 * p2
116	    ET2 = a1**2 * p1 + a2**2 * p2 + sigma_T**2
117	
118	    q = C @ p_A  # q[j] = P(A*=j)
119	
120	    # E[T * D*_j] = a1*C[j,1]*p1 + a2*C[j,2]*p2
121	    ET_Ds = np.array([a1 * C[j, 1] * p1 + a2 * C[j, 2] * p2 for j in range(3)])
122	
123	    # E[Z'Z]
124	    EZZ = np.array([
125	        [1.0,  ET,       q[1],      q[2]],
126	        [ET,   ET2,      ET_Ds[1],  ET_Ds[2]],
127	        [q[1], ET_Ds[1], q[1],      0.0],
128	        [q[2], ET_Ds[2], 0.0,       q[2]]
129	    ])
130	
131	    # E[Z'X]:  E[D*_j * D_k] = C[j,k]*p_k
132	    EZX = np.array([
133	        [1.0,  ET,       p1,             p2],
134	        [ET,   ET2,      a1 * p1,        a2 * p2],
135	        [q[1], ET_Ds[1], C[1, 1] * p1,   C[1, 2] * p2],
136	        [q[2], ET_Ds[2], C[2, 1] * p1,   C[2, 2] * p2]
137	    ])
138	
139	    plim = np.linalg.solve(EZZ, EZX @ beta)
140	    return plim[1] - beta_T, plim
141	
142	
143	def theoretical_bias_largesample(C_base, p_A, alpha, beta_T, beta_A,
144	                                  sigma_T, sigma_Y, N_approx=2_000_000,
145	                                  seed=999):
146	    """
147	    Approximate theoretical bias for differential misclassification
148	    via large-sample moment estimation.
149	    """
150	    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
151	    a1, a2 = alpha
152	
153	    A = rng.choice(3, size=N_approx, p=p_A)
154	    D1 = (A == 1).astype(np.float64)
155	    D2 = (A == 2).astype(np.float64)
156	    T = a1 * D1 + a2 * D2 + rng.normal(0, sigma_T, N_approx)
157	
158	    A_star = _generate_Astar_differential(A, T, C_base, rng)
159	    D1s = (A_star == 1).astype(np.float64)
160	    D2s = (A_star == 2).astype(np.float64)
161	
162	    beta = np.array([0.0, beta_T, beta_A[0], beta_A[1]])
163	
164	    ones = np.ones(N_approx)
165	    Z = np.column_stack([ones, T, D1s, D2s])
166	    X = np.column_stack([ones, T, D1, D2])
167	
168	    EZZ = (Z.T @ Z) / N_approx
169	    EZX = (Z.T @ X) / N_approx
170	
171	    plim = np.linalg.solve(EZZ, EZX @ beta)
172	    return plim[1] - beta_T, plim
173	
174	
175	# ============================================================
176	# Data generation
177	# ============================================================
178	def _generate_Astar_nondiff(A, C, rng):
179	    """Vectorized non-differential A* generation."""
180	    probs = C[:, A]                          # (3, N)
181	    cum = np.cumsum(probs, axis=0)           # (3, N)
182	    u = rng.uniform(size=A.shape[0])
183	    return ((u >= cum[0]).astype(int) + (u >= cum[1]).astype(int))
184	
185	
186	def _make_C_high(C_base, delta=0.15):
187	    """Reduce diagonal by delta, redistribute to off-diagonal."""
188	    C_high = C_base.copy()
189	    for col in range(3):
190	        reduction = min(delta, C_high[col, col] - 1.0 / 3.0)
191	        if reduction <= 0:
192	            continue
193	        C_high[col, col] -= reduction
194	        off = [j for j in range(3) if j != col]
195	        for j in off:
196	            C_high[j, col] += reduction / 2.0
197	    return C_high
198	
199	
200	def _generate_Astar_differential(A, T, C_base, rng):
201	    """T > median => higher misclassification rate."""
202	    N = len(A)
203	    C_high = _make_C_high(C_base)
204	    T_med = np.median(T)
205	    high = T > T_med
206	
207	    probs_low = C_base[:, A]     # (3, N)
208	    probs_high = C_high[:, A]    # (3, N)
209	    probs = np.where(high[np.newaxis, :], probs_high, probs_low)
210	
211	    cum = np.cumsum(probs, axis=0)
212	    u = rng.uniform(size=N)
213	    return ((u >= cum[0]).astype(int) + (u >= cum[1]).astype(int))
214	
215	
216	def generate_data(N, C, p_A, alpha, beta_T, beta_A, sigma_T, sigma_Y,
217	                  differential, rng):
218	    a1, a2 = alpha
219	    b1, b2 = beta_A
220	
221	    A = rng.choice(3, size=N, p=p_A)
222	    D1 = (A == 1).astype(np.float64)
223	    D2 = (A == 2).astype(np.float64)
224	    T = a1 * D1 + a2 * D2 + rng.normal(0, sigma_T, N)
225	    Y = beta_T * T + b1 * D1 + b2 * D2 + rng.normal(0, sigma_Y, N)
226	
227	    if differential:
228	        A_star = _generate_Astar_differential(A, T, C, rng)
229	    else:
230	        A_star = _generate_Astar_nondiff(A, C, rng)
231	
232	    return A, T, Y, A_star
233	
234	
235	# ============================================================
236	# OLS helper
237	# ============================================================
238	def ols_beta_T(T, Y, dummies):
239	    """OLS Y ~ 1 + T + dummies, return coefficient on T."""
240	    X = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(T)), T, dummies])
241	    coef, _, _, _ = np.linalg.lstsq(X, Y, rcond=None)
242	    return coef[1]
243	
244	
245	# ============================================================
246	# Monte Carlo
247	# ============================================================
248	def run_mc(M, N, C, p_A, alpha, beta_T, beta_A, sigma_T, sigma_Y,
249	           differential, seed):
250	    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
251	    bias_true = np.empty(M)
252	    bias_misclass = np.empty(M)
253	
254	    for m in range(M):
255	        A, T, Y, A_star = generate_data(
256	            N, C, p_A, alpha, beta_T, beta_A, sigma_T, sigma_Y,
257	            differential, rng
258	        )
259	        D_true = np.column_stack([(A == 1).astype(float), (A == 2).astype(float)])
260	        D_star = np.column_stack([(A_star == 1).astype(float),
261	                                   (A_star == 2).astype(float)])
262	        bias_true[m] = ols_beta_T(T, Y, D_true) - beta_T
263	        bias_misclass[m] = ols_beta_T(T, Y, D_star) - beta_T
264	
265	    return bias_true, bias_misclass
266	
267	
268	# ============================================================
269	# Unadjusted bias (omitted variable)
270	# ============================================================
271	def unadjusted_bias(p_A, alpha, beta_T, beta_A, sigma_T):
272	    """plim of OLS Y ~ 1 + T (no confounder control)."""
273	    p0, p1, p2 = p_A
274	    a1, a2 = alpha
275	    b1, b2 = beta_A
276	
277	    ET = a1 * p1 + a2 * p2
278	    VarT = a1**2 * p1 + a2**2 * p2 + sigma_T**2 - ET**2
279	    CovD1T = a1 * p1 - p1 * ET    # Cov(1[A=1], T)
280	    CovD2T = a2 * p2 - p2 * ET    # Cov(1[A=2], T)
281	    return (b1 * CovD1T + b2 * CovD2T) / VarT
282	
283	
284	# ============================================================
285	# Binary collapse analysis
286	# ============================================================
287	def collapse_binary_C(C, p_A):
288	    """
289	    Derive 2x2 confusion matrix for B=1[A in {1,2}] from 3x3 C.
290	
291	    C_bin[0,0] = P(B*=0|B=0) = C[0,0]
292	    C_bin[1,0] = P(B*=1|B=0) = C[1,0] + C[2,0]
293	    C_bin[0,1] = P(B*=0|B=1) = weighted avg of P(A*=0|A=1), P(A*=0|A=2)
294	    C_bin[1,1] = 1 - C_bin[0,1]
295	    """
296	    p1, p2 = p_A[1], p_A[2]
297	    pB1 = p1 + p2
298	
299	    c_bin_00 = C[0, 0]
300	    c_bin_10 = C[1, 0] + C[2, 0]
301	    c_bin_01 = (C[0, 1] * p1 + C[0, 2] * p2) / pB1
302	    c_bin_11 = 1.0 - c_bin_01
303	
304	    C_bin = np.array([[c_bin_00, c_bin_01],
305	                      [c_bin_10, c_bin_11]])
306	    return C_bin
307	
308	
309	def theoretical_bias_binary(C_bin, p_A, alpha, beta_T, beta_A, sigma_T):
310	    """
311	    Theoretical bias when collapsing to binary B=1[A in {1,2}].
312	    True model still has separate D1, D2 effects.
313	
314	    Z_bin = (1, T, B*),  X_full = (1, T, D1, D2)
315	    plim = (E[Z_bin'Z_bin])^{-1} E[Z_bin'X_full] beta
316	    """
317	    p0, p1, p2 = p_A
318	    a1, a2 = alpha
319	    b1, b2 = beta_A
320	    beta = np.array([0.0, beta_T, b1, b2])
321	    pB1 = p1 + p2
322	
323	    ET = a1 * p1 + a2 * p2
324	    ET2 = a1**2 * p1 + a2**2 * p2 + sigma_T**2
325	
326	    # P(B*=1) via confusion
327	    q_Bs1 = C_bin[1, 0] * p0 + C_bin[1, 1] * pB1
328	
329	    # E[T * B*] = E[T * 1[A* in {1,2}]]
330	    #   = sum_j in {1,2} E[T * D*_j]
331	    #   = sum_j in {1,2} (a1*C[j,1]*p1 + a2*C[j,2]*p2)
332	    # But we only have C_bin, so reconstruct:
333	    # E[T * B*] = E[T * E[B*|A,T]]
334	    # For non-diff: E[B*|A=0] = C_bin[1,0], E[B*|A=1,2] = C_bin[1,1]
335	    # E[T*B*] = C_bin[1,0]*E[T*1[A=0]] + C_bin[1,1]*E[T*1[A in {1,2}]]
336	    # E[T*1[A=0]] = E[T*D0] = 0*p0 = 0  (since T = a1*D1 + a2*D2 + eta, D0 uncorrelated w/ eta)
337	    # Wait: E[T*D0] = E[(a1*D1 + a2*D2 + eta)*D0] = 0 (D0*D1=0, D0*D2=0, E[eta*D0]=0)
338	    # E[T*B] = E[T*(D1+D2)] = a1*p1 + a2*p2
339	    ET_Bs = C_bin[1, 0] * 0.0 + C_bin[1, 1] * (a1 * p1 + a2 * p2)
340	
341	    # E[B* * D_k] for k=1,2
342	    # E[B* * D1] = P(B*=1, A=1) = P(A* in {1,2} | A=1)*p1
343	    #   = (1 - C[0,1])*p1 = (1 - P(A*=0|A=1))*p1
344	    # Using C_bin: P(B*=1|B=1) = C_bin[1,1], but this is averaged over A=1,2.

358	    and uses B* = 1[A* in {1,2}].

377	    ET_Ds = np.array([a1 * C[j, 1] * p1 + a2 * C[j, 2] * p2 for j in range(3)])

379

385	    ])
386

388	    # E[B* * D_k] = P(B*=1, A=k) = P(A* in {1,2} | A=k) * p_k
389	    #             = (C[1,k] + C[2,k]) * p_k  =  (1 - C[0,k]) * p_k
390	    EB_D1 = (1.0 - C[0, 1]) * p1

395	        [ET,     ET2,    a1 * p1,  a2 * p2],
396	        [q_Bs,   ET_Bs,  EB_D1,    EB_D2]
397	    ])
398

400	    return plim[1] - beta_T

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
MVP Validation: Confounding DAG with K=3 Multiclass Annotation Error

Verifies that multiclass (K>=3) annotation error in causal inference
produces qualitatively different bias patterns than binary misclassification.

DAG: A -> T, A -> Y, T -> Y
  A in {0,1,2}: true 3-class confounder
  A*: noisy annotation via 3x3 confusion matrix C
  T: continuous treatment
  Y: continuous outcome

DGP:
  T = alpha_1*1[A=1] + alpha_2*1[A=2] + eta,  eta ~ N(0, sigma_T^2)
  Y = beta_T*T + beta_1*1[A=1] + beta_2*1[A=2] + eps,  eps ~ N(0, sigma_Y^2)
  P(A*=j|A=i) = C[j,i]  (C is column-stochastic)

Key result: plim gamma_hat = (E[Z'Z])^{-1} E[Z'X] beta
  where Z uses A* dummies, X uses true A dummies.

Pass criteria:
  1. Theory vs MC 95% CI match: 5/5
  2. >=1 non-differential C produces away-from-null bias
  3. Binary collapse bias != multiclass theory prediction

Dependencies: numpy, scipy (standard library only)
"""

import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
import time

# ============================================================
# Configuration
# ============================================================
N_SAMPLES = 10_000
M_REPS = 1_000
SEED = 42

P_A = np.array([0.4, 0.35, 0.25])
ALPHA = np.array([1.5, -1.0])        # alpha_1, alpha_2
BETA_T = 2.0                          # true causal effect
BETA_A = np.array([1.0, -0.5])       # beta_1, beta_2
SIGMA_T = 1.0
SIGMA_Y = 1.0


# ============================================================
# Confusion matrix definitions
# ============================================================
def make_confusion_matrices():
    """5 confusion matrix structures. Each column sums to 1."""
    matrices = {}

    # 1. Symmetric high accuracy: diag=0.8, off-diag=0.1
    matrices["1_sym_high"] = (np.array([
        [0.80, 0.10, 0.10],
        [0.10, 0.80, 0.10],
        [0.10, 0.10, 0.80]
    ]), False)

    # 2. Asymmetric: P(A*=1|A=0)=0.30 >> P(A*=0|A=1)=0.05
    matrices["2_asymmetric"] = (np.array([
        [0.65, 0.05, 0.10],
        [0.30, 0.85, 0.10],
        [0.05, 0.10, 0.80]
    ]), False)

    # 3. Structural: classes 1<->2 heavily confused, class 0 clean
    matrices["3_struct_12"] = (np.array([
        [0.90, 0.05, 0.05],
        [0.05, 0.65, 0.30],
        [0.05, 0.30, 0.65]
    ]), False)

    # 4. Near-random: diag~0.4
    matrices["4_near_rand"] = (np.array([
        [0.40, 0.30, 0.30],
        [0.30, 0.40, 0.30],
        [0.30, 0.30, 0.40]
    ]), False)

    # 5. Differential: base C + T-dependent error increase
    matrices["5_differen"] = (np.array([
        [0.80, 0.10, 0.10],
        [0.10, 0.80, 0.10],
        [0.10, 0.10, 0.80]
    ]), True)

    for name, (C, _) in matrices.items():
        assert np.allclose(C.sum(axis=0), 1.0), f"{name}: columns don't sum to 1"
        assert (C >= 0).all(), f"{name}: negative entries"

    return matrices


# ============================================================
# Theoretical bias (exact, for non-differential C)
# ============================================================
def theoretical_bias_exact(C, p_A, alpha, beta_T, beta_A, sigma_T):
    """
    Compute plim of OLS with misclassified A* dummies.

    plim gamma = (E[Z'Z])^{-1} E[Z'X] beta
    Z = (1, T, D*_1, D*_2),  X = (1, T, D_1, D_2)

    Returns: (bias_on_betaT, full_plim_vector)
    """
    p0, p1, p2 = p_A
    a1, a2 = alpha
    b1, b2 = beta_A
    beta = np.array([0.0, beta_T, b1, b2])

    ET = a1 * p1 + a2 * p2
    ET2 = a1**2 * p1 + a2**2 * p2 + sigma_T**2

    q = C @ p_A  # q[j] = P(A*=j)

    # E[T * D*_j] = a1*C[j,1]*p1 + a2*C[j,2]*p2
    ET_Ds = np.array([a1 * C[j, 1] * p1 + a2 * C[j, 2] * p2 for j in range(3)])

    # E[Z'Z]
    EZZ = np.array([
        [1.0,  ET,       q[1],      q[2]],
        [ET,   ET2,      ET_Ds[1],  ET_Ds[2]],
        [q[1], ET_Ds[1], q[1],      0.0],
        [q[2], ET_Ds[2], 0.0,       q[2]]
    ])

    # E[Z'X]:  E[D*_j * D_k] = C[j,k]*p_k
    EZX = np.array([
        [1.0,  ET,       p1,             p2],
        [ET,   ET2,      a1 * p1,        a2 * p2],
        [q[1], ET_Ds[1], C[1, 1] * p1,   C[1, 2] * p2],
        [q[2], ET_Ds[2], C[2, 1] * p1,   C[2, 2] * p2]
    ])

    plim = np.linalg.solve(EZZ, EZX @ beta)
    return plim[1] - beta_T, plim


def theoretical_bias_largesample(C_base, p_A, alpha, beta_T, beta_A,
                                  sigma_T, sigma_Y, N_approx=2_000_000,
                                  seed=999):
    """
    Approximate theoretical bias for differential misclassification
    via large-sample moment estimation.
    """
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    a1, a2 = alpha

    A = rng.choice(3, size=N_approx, p=p_A)
    D1 = (A == 1).astype(np.float64)
    D2 = (A == 2).astype(np.float64)
    T = a1 * D1 + a2 * D2 + rng.normal(0, sigma_T, N_approx)

    A_star = _generate_Astar_differential(A, T, C_base, rng)
    D1s = (A_star == 1).astype(np.float64)
    D2s = (A_star == 2).astype(np.float64)

    beta = np.array([0.0, beta_T, beta_A[0], beta_A[1]])

    ones = np.ones(N_approx)
    Z = np.column_stack([ones, T, D1s, D2s])
    X = np.column_stack([ones, T, D1, D2])

    EZZ = (Z.T @ Z) / N_approx
    EZX = (Z.T @ X) / N_approx

    plim = np.linalg.solve(EZZ, EZX @ beta)
    return plim[1] - beta_T, plim


# ============================================================
# Data generation
# ============================================================
def _generate_Astar_nondiff(A, C, rng):
    """Vectorized non-differential A* generation."""
    probs = C[:, A]                          # (3, N)
    cum = np.cumsum(probs, axis=0)           # (3, N)
    u = rng.uniform(size=A.shape[0])
    return ((u >= cum[0]).astype(int) + (u >= cum[1]).astype(int))


def _make_C_high(C_base, delta=0.15):
    """Reduce diagonal by delta, redistribute to off-diagonal."""
    C_high = C_base.copy()
    for col in range(3):
        reduction = min(delta, C_high[col, col] - 1.0 / 3.0)
        if reduction <= 0:
            continue
        C_high[col, col] -= reduction
        off = [j for j in range(3) if j != col]
        for j in off:
            C_high[j, col] += reduction / 2.0
    return C_high


def _generate_Astar_differential(A, T, C_base, rng):
    """T > median => higher misclassification rate."""
    N = len(A)
    C_high = _make_C_high(C_base)
    T_med = np.median(T)
    high = T > T_med

    probs_low = C_base[:, A]     # (3, N)
    probs_high = C_high[:, A]    # (3, N)
    probs = np.where(high[np.newaxis, :], probs_high, probs_low)

    cum = np.cumsum(probs, axis=0)
    u = rng.uniform(size=N)
    return ((u >= cum[0]).astype(int) + (u >= cum[1]).astype(int))


def generate_data(N, C, p_A, alpha, beta_T, beta_A, sigma_T, sigma_Y,
                  differential, rng):
    a1, a2 = alpha
    b1, b2 = beta_A

    A = rng.choice(3, size=N, p=p_A)
    D1 = (A == 1).astype(np.float64)
    D2 = (A == 2).astype(np.float64)
    T = a1 * D1 + a2 * D2 + rng.normal(0, sigma_T, N)
    Y = beta_T * T + b1 * D1 + b2 * D2 + rng.normal(0, sigma_Y, N)

    if differential:
        A_star = _generate_Astar_differential(A, T, C, rng)
    else:
        A_star = _generate_Astar_nondiff(A, C, rng)

    return A, T, Y, A_star


# ============================================================
# OLS helper
# ============================================================
def ols_beta_T(T, Y, dummies):
    """OLS Y ~ 1 + T + dummies, return coefficient on T."""
    X = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(T)), T, dummies])
    coef, _, _, _ = np.linalg.lstsq(X, Y, rcond=None)
    return coef[1]


# ============================================================
# Monte Carlo
# ============================================================
def run_mc(M, N, C, p_A, alpha, beta_T, beta_A, sigma_T, sigma_Y,
           differential, seed):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    bias_true = np.empty(M)
    bias_misclass = np.empty(M)

    for m in range(M):
        A, T, Y, A_star = generate_data(
            N, C, p_A, alpha, beta_T, beta_A, sigma_T, sigma_Y,
            differential, rng
        )
        D_true = np.column_stack([(A == 1).astype(float), (A == 2).astype(float)])
        D_star = np.column_stack([(A_star == 1).astype(float),
                                   (A_star == 2).astype(float)])
        bias_true[m] = ols_beta_T(T, Y, D_true) - beta_T
        bias_misclass[m] = ols_beta_T(T, Y, D_star) - beta_T

    return bias_true, bias_misclass


# ============================================================
# Unadjusted bias (omitted variable)
# ============================================================
def unadjusted_bias(p_A, alpha, beta_T, beta_A, sigma_T):
    """plim of OLS Y ~ 1 + T (no confounder control)."""
    p0, p1, p2 = p_A
    a1, a2 = alpha
    b1, b2 = beta_A

    ET = a1 * p1 + a2 * p2
    VarT = a1**2 * p1 + a2**2 * p2 + sigma_T**2 - ET**2
    CovD1T = a1 * p1 - p1 * ET    # Cov(1[A=1], T)
    CovD2T = a2 * p2 - p2 * ET    # Cov(1[A=2], T)
    return (b1 * CovD1T + b2 * CovD2T) / VarT


# ============================================================
# Binary collapse analysis
# ============================================================
def collapse_binary_C(C, p_A):
    """
    Derive 2x2 confusion matrix for B=1[A in {1,2}] from 3x3 C.

    C_bin[0,0] = P(B*=0|B=0) = C[0,0]
    C_bin[1,0] = P(B*=1|B=0) = C[1,0] + C[2,0]
    C_bin[0,1] = P(B*=0|B=1) = weighted avg of P(A*=0|A=1), P(A*=0|A=2)
    C_bin[1,1] = 1 - C_bin[0,1]
    """
    p1, p2 = p_A[1], p_A[2]
    pB1 = p1 + p2

    c_bin_00 = C[0, 0]
    c_bin_10 = C[1, 0] + C[2, 0]
    c_bin_01 = (C[0, 1] * p1 + C[0, 2] * p2) / pB1
    c_bin_11 = 1.0 - c_bin_01

    C_bin = np.array([[c_bin_00, c_bin_01],
                      [c_bin_10, c_bin_11]])
    return C_bin


def theoretical_bias_binary(C_bin, p_A, alpha, beta_T, beta_A, sigma_T):
    """
    Theoretical bias when collapsing to binary B=1[A in {1,2}].
    True model still has separate D1, D2 effects.

    Z_bin = (1, T, B*),  X_full = (1, T, D1, D2)
    plim = (E[Z_bin'Z_bin])^{-1} E[Z_bin'X_full] beta
    """
    p0, p1, p2 = p_A
    a1, a2 = alpha
    b1, b2 = beta_A
    beta = np.array([0.0, beta_T, b1, b2])
    pB1 = p1 + p2

    ET = a1 * p1 + a2 * p2
    ET2 = a1**2 * p1 + a2**2 * p2 + sigma_T**2

    # P(B*=1) via confusion
    q_Bs1 = C_bin[1, 0] * p0 + C_bin[1, 1] * pB1

    # E[T * B*] = E[T * 1[A* in {1,2}]]
    #   = sum_j in {1,2} E[T * D*_j]
    #   = sum_j in {1,2} (a1*C[j,1]*p1 + a2*C[j,2]*p2)
    # But we only have C_bin, so reconstruct:
    # E[T * B*] = E[T * E[B*|A,T]]
    # For non-diff: E[B*|A=0] = C_bin[1,0], E[B*|A=1,2] = C_bin[1,1]
    # E[T*B*] = C_bin[1,0]*E[T*1[A=0]] + C_bin[1,1]*E[T*1[A in {1,2}]]
    # E[T*1[A=0]] = E[T*D0] = 0*p0 = 0  (since T = a1*D1 + a2*D2 + eta, D0 uncorrelated w/ eta)
    # Wait: E[T*D0] = E[(a1*D1 + a2*D2 + eta)*D0] = 0 (D0*D1=0, D0*D2=0, E[eta*D0]=0)
    # E[T*B] = E[T*(D1+D2)] = a1*p1 + a2*p2
    ET_Bs = C_bin[1, 0] * 0.0 + C_bin[1, 1] * (a1 * p1 + a2 * p2)

    # E[B* * D_k] for k=1,2
    # E[B* * D1] = P(B*=1, A=1) = P(A* in {1,2} | A=1)*p1
    #   = (1 - C[0,1])*p1 = (1 - P(A*=0|A=1))*p1
    # Using C_bin: P(B*=1|B=1) = C_bin[1,1], but this is averaged over A=1,2.
    # More precisely: P(B*=1|A=1) = 1 - C[0,1] (from original 3x3 C)
    # We don't have the original C here, so let's pass it separately.
    # Actually, let's just compute this from the original C.
    # This function should receive the original C too, or compute directly.
    # Let me restructure...

    # For cleanliness, compute binary plim from original C directly.
    raise NotImplementedError("Use theoretical_bias_binary_from_C3 instead")


def theoretical_bias_binary_from_C3(C, p_A, alpha, beta_T, beta_A, sigma_T):
    """
    Theoretical bias when researcher collapses A to B=1[A in {1,2}]
    and uses B* = 1[A* in {1,2}].

    Z = (1, T, B*),  X = (1, T, D1, D2)
    plim = (E[Z'Z])^{-1} E[Z'X] beta
    """
    p0, p1, p2 = p_A
    a1, a2 = alpha
    b1, b2 = beta_A
    beta = np.array([0.0, beta_T, b1, b2])

    ET = a1 * p1 + a2 * p2
    ET2 = a1**2 * p1 + a2**2 * p2 + sigma_T**2

    # B* = 1[A* in {1,2}] = D*_1 + D*_2
    # P(B*=1) = sum_{j=1,2} q_j where q_j = sum_i C[j,i]*p_i
    q = C @ p_A
    q_Bs = q[1] + q[2]  # = 1 - q[0]

    # E[T * B*] = E[T*(D*1 + D*2)] = sum_{j=1,2} E[T*D*_j]
    ET_Ds = np.array([a1 * C[j, 1] * p1 + a2 * C[j, 2] * p2 for j in range(3)])
    ET_Bs = ET_Ds[1] + ET_Ds[2]

    # E[Z'Z]: Z = (1, T, B*)
    EZZ = np.array([
        [1.0,    ET,    q_Bs],
        [ET,     ET2,   ET_Bs],
        [q_Bs,   ET_Bs, q_Bs]    # B*^2 = B* (indicator)
    ])

    # E[Z'X]: X = (1, T, D1, D2)
    # E[B* * D_k] = P(B*=1, A=k) = P(A* in {1,2} | A=k) * p_k
    #             = (C[1,k] + C[2,k]) * p_k  =  (1 - C[0,k]) * p_k
    EB_D1 = (1.0 - C[0, 1]) * p1
    EB_D2 = (1.0 - C[0, 2]) * p2

    EZX = np.array([
        [1.0,    ET,     p1,       p2],
        [ET,     ET2,    a1 * p1,  a2 * p2],
        [q_Bs,   ET_Bs,  EB_D1,    EB_D2]
    ])

    plim = np.linalg.solve(EZZ, EZX @ beta)
    return plim[1] - beta_T


def run_mc_binary_collapse(M, N, C, p_A, alpha, beta_T, beta_A,
                           sigma_T, sigma_Y, differential, seed):
    """MC with binary collapse: B=1[A in {1,2}], B*=1[A* in {1,2}]."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    bias_bin = np.empty(M)

    for m in range(M):
        A, T, Y, A_star = generate_data(
            N, C, p_A, alpha, beta_T, beta_A, sigma_T, sigma_Y,
            differential, rng
        )
        B_star = ((A_star == 1) | (A_star == 2)).astype(float).reshape(-1, 1)
        bias_bin[m] = ols_beta_T(T, Y, B_star) - beta_T

    return bias_bin


# ============================================================
# Main
# ============================================================
def main():
    print("=" * 80)
    print("MVP Validation: Confounding DAG — K=3 Multiclass Annotation Error Bias")
    print("=" * 80)
    print(f"\nDGP: P(A)={list(P_A)}, alpha={list(ALPHA)}, "
          f"beta_T={BETA_T}, beta_A={list(BETA_A)}")
    print(f"     sigma_T={SIGMA_T}, sigma_Y={SIGMA_Y}")
    print(f"MC:  N={N_SAMPLES:,}, M={M_REPS:,}, seed={SEED}")

    # Unadjusted bias (omitted variable reference)
    ovb = unadjusted_bias(P_A, ALPHA, BETA_T, BETA_A, SIGMA_T)
    print(f"\nUnadjusted OVB (no A control): {ovb:.6f}")
    print(f"  => Unadjusted plim(beta_T_hat) = {BETA_T + ovb:.6f}")
    print(f"  => Direction: {'toward null' if ovb * BETA_T < 0 else 'away from null'}")

    matrices = make_confusion_matrices()

    # ── Step 1-3: K=3 analysis ──────────────────────────────
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PART A: K=3 Multiclass — Theory vs Monte Carlo")
    print("=" * 80)

    results_k3 = {}
    header = f"{'Config':<14} {'Theory':>10} {'MC Mean':>10} {'MC 95% CI':>22} {'Match?':>7} {'Dir':>14}"
    print(f"\n{header}")
    print("-" * len(header))

    for name, (C, is_diff) in matrices.items():
        t0 = time.time()

        # Theoretical bias
        if is_diff:
            th_bias, _ = theoretical_bias_largesample(
                C, P_A, ALPHA, BETA_T, BETA_A, SIGMA_T, SIGMA_Y)
        else:
            th_bias, _ = theoretical_bias_exact(
                C, P_A, ALPHA, BETA_T, BETA_A, SIGMA_T)

        # Monte Carlo
        _, mc_bias = run_mc(M_REPS, N_SAMPLES, C, P_A, ALPHA, BETA_T,
                            BETA_A, SIGMA_T, SIGMA_Y, is_diff, SEED)

        mc_mean = mc_bias.mean()
        mc_se = mc_bias.std(ddof=1)
        ci_lo = mc_mean - 1.96 * mc_se / np.sqrt(M_REPS)
        ci_hi = mc_mean + 1.96 * mc_se / np.sqrt(M_REPS)
        match = ci_lo <= th_bias <= ci_hi

        # Direction relative to null
        if abs(th_bias) < 1e-6:
            direction = "~zero"
        elif th_bias * BETA_T > 0:
            direction = "AWAY from null"
        else:
            direction = "toward null"

        elapsed = time.time() - t0
        results_k3[name] = {
            "th_bias": th_bias, "mc_mean": mc_mean,
            "ci": (ci_lo, ci_hi), "match": match,
            "direction": direction, "mc_bias_arr": mc_bias,
            "is_diff": is_diff
        }

        print(f"{name:<14} {th_bias:>10.6f} {mc_mean:>10.6f} "
              f"[{ci_lo:>9.6f}, {ci_hi:>9.6f}] {'YES' if match else '**NO**':>7} "
              f"{direction:>14}  ({elapsed:.1f}s)")

    # ── Step 4: Binary collapse ──────────────────────────────
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PART B: Binary Collapse — B=1[A in {1,2}]")
    print("=" * 80)

    header_b = (f"{'Config':<14} {'K3 Theory':>10} {'Bin Theory':>10} "
                f"{'Bin MC Mean':>11} {'Bin MC 95% CI':>22} {'K3!=Bin?':>8}")
    print(f"\n{header_b}")
    print("-" * len(header_b))

    pass_criterion_3 = False

    for name, (C, is_diff) in matrices.items():
        t0 = time.time()
        k3_bias = results_k3[name]["th_bias"]

        # Binary theoretical (from original 3x3 C, non-differential only)
        if not is_diff:
            bin_th = theoretical_bias_binary_from_C3(
                C, P_A, ALPHA, BETA_T, BETA_A, SIGMA_T)
        else:
            # For differential, use large-sample approx for binary too
            rng_approx = np.random.default_rng(888)
            N_ap = 2_000_000
            A_ap = rng_approx.choice(3, size=N_ap, p=P_A)
            D1_ap = (A_ap == 1).astype(np.float64)
            D2_ap = (A_ap == 2).astype(np.float64)
            T_ap = ALPHA[0] * D1_ap + ALPHA[1] * D2_ap + rng_approx.normal(0, SIGMA_T, N_ap)
            As_ap = _generate_Astar_differential(A_ap, T_ap, C, rng_approx)
            Bs_ap = ((As_ap == 1) | (As_ap == 2)).astype(np.float64)
            beta_vec = np.array([0.0, BETA_T, BETA_A[0], BETA_A[1]])
            ones_ap = np.ones(N_ap)
            Z_b = np.column_stack([ones_ap, T_ap, Bs_ap])
            X_f = np.column_stack([ones_ap, T_ap, D1_ap, D2_ap])
            EZZ_b = (Z_b.T @ Z_b) / N_ap
            EZX_b = (Z_b.T @ X_f) / N_ap
            plim_b = np.linalg.solve(EZZ_b, EZX_b @ beta_vec)
            bin_th = plim_b[1] - BETA_T

        # Binary MC
        bin_mc = run_mc_binary_collapse(
            M_REPS, N_SAMPLES, C, P_A, ALPHA, BETA_T, BETA_A,
            SIGMA_T, SIGMA_Y, is_diff, SEED)

        bin_mean = bin_mc.mean()
        bin_se = bin_mc.std(ddof=1)
        bin_ci_lo = bin_mean - 1.96 * bin_se / np.sqrt(M_REPS)
        bin_ci_hi = bin_mean + 1.96 * bin_se / np.sqrt(M_REPS)

        k3_ne_bin = abs(k3_bias - bin_th) > 0.001
        if k3_ne_bin:
            pass_criterion_3 = True

        elapsed = time.time() - t0
        print(f"{name:<14} {k3_bias:>10.6f} {bin_th:>10.6f} "
              f"{bin_mean:>11.6f} [{bin_ci_lo:>9.6f}, {bin_ci_hi:>9.6f}] "
              f"{'YES' if k3_ne_bin else 'no':>8}  ({elapsed:.1f}s)")

    # ── Pass/Fail summary ────────────────────────────────────
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PASS / FAIL SUMMARY")
    print("=" * 80)

    # Criterion 1: all 5 theory-MC matches
    n_match = sum(1 for r in results_k3.values() if r["match"])
    c1 = n_match == 5
    print(f"\n1. Theory vs MC 95% CI match: {n_match}/5  "
          f"{'PASS' if c1 else 'FAIL'}")

    # Criterion 2: >=1 non-differential C with away-from-null bias
    away_nondiff = [name for name, r in results_k3.items()
                    if not r["is_diff"] and r["direction"] == "AWAY from null"]
    c2 = len(away_nondiff) >= 1
    print(f"2. Non-diff C with away-from-null bias: {len(away_nondiff)} "
          f"({', '.join(away_nondiff) if away_nondiff else 'none'})  "
          f"{'PASS' if c2 else 'FAIL'}")

    # Criterion 3: binary collapse != multiclass
    print(f"3. Binary collapse bias != K=3 theory: "
          f"{'PASS' if pass_criterion_3 else 'FAIL'}")

    print(f"\nOVERALL: {'PASS' if (c1 and c2 and pass_criterion_3) else 'FAIL'}")

    # ── Detailed confusion matrices ──────────────────────────
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("APPENDIX: Confusion Matrices")
    print("=" * 80)
    for name, (C, is_diff) in matrices.items():
        tag = " [DIFFERENTIAL]" if is_diff else ""
        print(f"\n{name}{tag}:")
        for row in C:
            print(f"  [{row[0]:.2f}  {row[1]:.2f}  {row[2]:.2f}]")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

[severity: warning] MVP 结果验证 — Confounding DAG K=3

**结论**: 有条件 PASS，但 criterion 2 的解读存在概念性问题，需在进入 research 阶段前明确。

---

### 逐项回应 Director 三个问题

**Q1: 100k 随机 C 搜索无方向反转——confounding DAG 是否本质单调？**

是的，这是预期结果，不是 negative result。在 confounding DAG（A→T, A→Y, T→Y）中，A* 替代 A 做调整本质上是**部分调整**——用噪声代理控制混杂，只能减少调整质量，不能"过度调整"到反方向。这在流行病学中是已知性质（Greenland 1980; Ogburn & VanderWeele 2012）：非差异性混杂因素误分类产生的残余混杂始终与原始混杂方向一致。

100k 搜索确认了这一单调性在 K=3 下仍成立——这本身是一个有价值的 characterization result（"confounding DAG 偏差方向可预测"），应当纳入论文。**但这不是"多分类打破二分类保证"的证据**——见 Q2。

**Q2: 所有非差异性 C 产生正偏差 0.20-0.30 是预期行为？criterion 2 解读是否正确？**

[severity: warning] **解读部分正确，但 criterion 2 存在概念偷换。**

ROADMAP 核心假设原文："二分类中非差异性误分类保证偏差方向向零（bias toward null），但多分类中此保证不成立"。这里的 "bias toward null" 是关于**暴露变量（exposure）误分类**的经典结论（Bross 1954; Copeland et al. 1977），不是关于混杂因素（confounder）误分类。

对于 **confounder** 误分类，即使在二分类中，非差异性误分类也产生远离零偏差（residual confounding，方向与 OVB 一致）。所以 criterion 2（"≥1 种非差异性 C 产生远离零偏差"）在 confounding DAG 下**对二分类也是 PASS 的**——它没有区分二分类和多分类。

真正体现多分类差异的是：
- **Criterion 3**（二分类折叠不等价）——这是 MVP 的实质贡献
- **方向反转**需要在 **exposure misclassification DAG**（如 A→Y，直接用 A* 替代 A）或 **mediator DAG** 中验证

**实际影响**：MVP 证明了理论框架可行（criterion 1）和折叠损失真实存在（criterion 3），但没有验证核心 claim 中最有 punch 的部分（方向反转/bias-toward-null 保证打破）。这部分必须在 research 阶段的 exposure/mediator DAG 拓扑中完成。

**Q3: 是否可以 complete_mvp 进入 research？**

**可以，但附加条件**：

1. Research 阶段第一优先级必须是 **exposure misclassification DAG（A→Y，A* 替代 A 估计 A 对 Y 的因果效应）的 K=3 验证**——这才是"bias toward null breaks"的正确测试场景。如果此 DAG 也无法产生方向反转，核心 claim 需要重新框定。

2. Decisions.yaml D001 中的表述"所有非差异性 C 产生远离零偏差 0.20-0.30"不应被引用为"打破二分类保证"的证据。应修正为"confounding DAG 单调性验证 + 折叠损失验证"。

3. 100k 随机搜索的代码不在 artifact 中，registry 也为空（Agent 未将实验注册到 registry）。这违反了实验追溯审查要求：**结果不可独立复现**。建议 Agent 将完整代码（含 100k 搜索）+ 输出日志注册到 registry。

### 总结

MVP 通过 criterion 1 和 3 证明了技术框架的有效性，criterion 2 在 confounding DAG 下不具有区分力。进入 research 阶段合理，但方向反转（核心 claim 最强部分）的验证尚未完成，需立即在 exposure DAG 拓扑中补充。

## 核心方向
多分类 LLM 标注误差在因果推断中的偏差传播：推导 K×K 混淆矩阵在 6 种 DAG 拓扑下的偏差表达式，构建 Annotation Sensitivity Values (ASVs) 灵敏度分析框架。详见 paper_framing.md。

Confounding DAG + K=3 验证通过。理论框架正确（5/5 MC 匹配），多分类≠二分类已量化（Δ≤0.089）。Confounding DAG 偏差单调向 OVB（100k 随机 C 无方向反转）。方向反转需在其他拓扑验证。

- Primary: AAAI 2027（abstract 2026-07-21, paper 2026-07-28）
- Secondary: ARR October 2026（→ NAACL/ACL 2027）

### Core Claims（详见 paper_framing.md）
1. Multi-class bias taxonomy — 6 DAG 拓扑 × K×K 混淆矩阵结构交互
2. Annotation Sensitivity Values (ASVs) — 标注误差灵敏度分析
3. Correction guidance framework — 诊断驱动的纠偏方法选择

### 实验覆盖（详见 experiment_plan.yaml，compute_coverage_matrix 派生）
- P0 (必跑): plan_001(6 DAG K=3), plan_003(3 LLM实证), plan_004(ASV证明), plan_006(ASV实证), plan_008(二分类折叠)
- P1 (重要): plan_002(K=5,7), plan_005(ASV扩展), plan_007(纠偏框架), plan_010(工具包)
- P2 (加分): plan_009(病态C分析)

## 当前进展
- ✅ MVP 通过（D001）
- ✅ paper_framing.md 已写
- ✅ experiment_plan.yaml 已写

## GPU 预算
本项目 GPU 需求极低（总计 15-30h，后期 LLM API 实证用）。当前 0 GPU 分配。
服务器：home-1x5090（sonny），已绑定。

content.content: {"result":"{\"success\": true, \"data\": {\"path\": \"/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-prod_0510/projects/causal_annot_error_attrib/paper_framing.md\", \"content\": \"# Paper Framing — causal_annot_error_attrib\\n\\n## Target Venue\\n- Primary: AAAI 2027 (abstract: 2026-07-21, paper: 2026-07-28)\\n- Secondary: ARR October 2026 (~2026-10-15, commit to NAACL 2027 / ACL 2027)\\n- Tertiary: ICWSM 2027 Round 2 (2026-09-15)\\n\\n## Title\\nMulti-Class Annotation Errors Are Not Created Equal: Bias Taxonomy, Sensitivity Analysis, and Correction Guidance for LLM-Annotated Causal Studies\\n\\n## Core Claims (3 条)\\n\\n1. **Multi-class bias taxonomy**: For K≥3 annotation variables, the direction and magnitude of downstream bias depend on the interaction between the K×K confusion matrix structure and the DAG topology — breaking guarantees that hold in the binary case. We provide closed-form bias expressions for K=3 and matrix-form expressions with interpretability tools for general K, across 6 canonical social-science DAG topologies (confounding, mediation, collider, M-bias, instrument, front-door).\\n\\n2. **Annotation Sensitivity Values (ASVs)**: A sensitivity analysis framework for annotation-induced bias. ASVs quantify the minimum degree of differential annotation error needed to overturn a downstream conclusion, parameterized by a reference confusion matrix and amplification factor δ. Reported alongside estimates, analogous to E-values for unmeasured confounding. Formal proofs (monotonicity + sharpness) for 3 priority topologies; MC-validated conjectures for the remaining 3.\\n\\n3. **Correction guidance framework**: A principled decision framework mapping {DAG topology × error structure × ASV} to the appropriate correction method (DSL, PPI, MLA, naive plug-in), characterizing regimes where each applies and where no existing method suffices — including dependence-aware multi-LLM correction as an open problem.\\n\\n## Story Spine\\n\\n- **Problem**: LLMs are rapidly replacing human annotators in CSS, but Baumann et al. (2025) show 31% of downstream conclusions are already incorrect. Researchers lack diagnostic tools to answer: (a) which annotation error structures propagate bias under their causal design, and (b) how robust their conclusions are to annotation error. Kim et al. (ICML 2025) show cross-model errors are highly correlated (60% agreement when both err), meaning ensembles cannot escape systematic bias — researchers MUST analyze the error structure of their chosen annotator, which is exactly what our tools enable.\\n\\n- **Existing approaches & gaps**: Wood-Doughty et al. (2018) apply DAG reasoning to text classifier errors but produce no formal bias theorems (binary only). TeBlunthuis et al. (2024) provide the most complete binary treatment with MLA correction but are limited to K=2, single classifier. Lee & Wood-Doughty (2024) extend to categorical + LLM classifiers but cover only 1 DAG topology (unobserved confounding), with no systematic taxonomy or sensitivity analysis. VanderWeele & Li (2019) provide sensitivity bounds but only for binary risk ratios. Jerzak et al. (EMNLP 2025) benchmark correction methods but treat error as monolithic — if different confusion matrix structures produce qualitatively different bias in different DAG topologies, unconditional benchmarking is itself misleading.\\n\\n- **Our framing**: Multi-class annotation errors are not created equal. The same confusion matrix that produces innocuous residual bias in one DAG topology can produce direction-reversing toxic bias in another. We provide the first systematic characterization of this interaction (the taxonomy), a tool to quantify robustness (ASVs), and guidance for when/how to correct (the framework). This is not a new correction method — it is the missing diagnostic layer that tells researchers which correction is appropriate, or whether correction is needed at all.\\n\\n- **Headline result template**: \\\"Across 6 DAG topologies with K=3,5,7, our bias expressions correctly predict bias direction and magnitude within 95% MC confidence intervals. On 3 CSS tasks annotated by 3 LLMs, ASVs provide calibrated robustness indicators, and our taxonomy identifies cases where commonly applied corrections would increase rather than decrease bias.\\\"\\n\\n## Core Insight (Lead Finding)\\n\\nThe binary guarantee that \\\"non-differential misclassification biases toward the null\\\" breaks in the multi-class case (Brenner 1993). But Brenner only identifies the danger without resolving the ambiguity. Our taxonomy resolves it: for each {confusion matrix structure × DAG topology} cell, we provide exact conditions determining when bias attenuates, amplifies, or reverses. Furthermore, the natural \\\"fix\\\" of binarizing a K-class variable is itself hazardous — collapsing categories introduces new, direction-unpredictable bias (demonstrated in MVP: Δ up to 0.089 between K=3 and binarized estimates).\\n\\n## MVP Evidence\\n\\nConfounding DAG + K=3 validated:\\n- Theoretical bias expressions match MC perfectly (5/5 structures within 95% CI)\\n- All non-differential C structures produce positive bias 0.20-0.30 (toward OVB)\\n- Binary collapse produces different bias (max Δ=0.089)\\n- 100k random C search: confounding DAG bias is monotonically toward OVB (no direction reversal in this topology)\\n- Direction reversal expected in mediator/collider topologies — research phase priority\\n\\n## Venue Fit Risks\\n\\n- **AAAI**: Broad AI audience — emphasize general methodology for \\\"automated annotation measurement error,\\\" not LLM-specific. Frame as extending classical measurement error theory to modern automated labeling.\\n- **ARR/NAACL**: NLP audience — CSS track is natural fit. May want more empirical NLP experiments. Balance theory with practical LLM annotation scenarios.\\n- **Cross-discipline bridge**: Epidemiology (measurement error theory) × NLP (annotation errors). Epi reviewers check proof rigor; NLP reviewers check empirical relevance. Must serve both.\\n\\n## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns & Planned Responses\\n\\n1. **\\\"Trivial extension of binary to multi-class\\\"** → Brenner (1993) proved direction reversal; our taxonomy provides the first systematic characterization across 6 topologies. Binarizing K-class introduces NEW unpredictable bias (MVP evidence). The complexity jump is structural: binary has 2 free parameters (sensitivity, specificity) → scalar bias; K=5 has 20 free parameters → matrix-valued bias requiring eigendecomposition for interpretation. [Experiments: plan_001, plan_008]\\n\\n2. **\\\"Lee & Wood-Doughty (2024) already did categorical\\\"** → They cover 1 topology (unobserved confounding) on 1 dataset (MIMIC). We cover 6 topologies with systematic taxonomy + ASVs + correction guidance. Their work is a stepping stone; ours is the full framework. [Experiments: plan_001]\\n\\n3. **\\\"Why these 6 DAG topologies?\\\"** → These are the canonical CSS causal designs used by Hernán & Cole (2009) and TeBlunthuis et al. (2024). They cover the major roles an annotated variable can play: confounder, mediator, collider, instrument, front-door criterion variable. [Experiments: plan_001]\\n\\n4. **\\\"K≥5 expressions aren't actionable\\\"** → Three interpretability tools: (a) eigendecomposition summaries identifying dominant bias modes, (b) worst-case scalar bounds, (c) diagnostic visualizations. [Experiments: plan_002]\\n\\n5. **\\\"ASV sharpness only proved for 3 topologies\\\"** → Honest scoping reflecting algebraic complexity. Remaining 3 validated via MC with numerical sharpness evidence. Full proofs identified as immediate future work. [Experiments: plan_004, plan_005]\\n\\n6. **\\\"Correlated multi-LLM errors?\\\"** → Kim et al. (ICML 2025) actually STRENGTHENS our case: if ensembles can't fix errors (60% agreement when both err), error structure analysis is the only viable approach. Multi-annotator correction with dependence is identified as an open problem. [Framework discussion]\\n\\n7. **\\\"Empirical validation scope\\\"** → 3 CSS tasks × 3 LLMs × 3 DAG-relevant scenarios. Tasks selected to cover K=2,3,5 annotation complexity. [Experiments: plan_003, plan_006]\\n\", \"total_chars\": 7854, \"truncated\": false}, \"error\": null, \"metadata\": {}}"}

## Target Venue
- Primary: AAAI 2027 (abstract: 2026-07-21, paper: 2026-07-28)
- Secondary: ARR October 2026 (~2026-10-15, commit to NAACL 2027 / ACL 2027)
- Tertiary: ICWSM 2027 Round 2 (2026-09-15)

## Title
Multi-Class Annotation Errors Are Not Created Equal: Bias Taxonomy, Sensitivity Analysis, and Correction Guidance for LLM-Annotated Causal Studies

## Core Claims (3 条)

1. **Multi-class bias taxonomy**: For K≥3 annotation variables, the direction and magnitude of downstream bias depend on the interaction between the K×K confusion matrix structure and the DAG topology — breaking guarantees that hold in the binary case. We provide closed-form bias expressions for K=3 and matrix-form expressions with interpretability tools for general K, across 6 canonical social-science DAG topologies (confounding, mediation, collider, M-bias, instrument, front-door).

2. **Annotation Sensitivity Values (ASVs)**: A sensitivity analysis framework for annotation-induced bias. ASVs quantify the minimum degree of differential annotation error needed to overturn a downstream conclusion, parameterized by a reference confusion matrix and amplification factor δ. Reported alongside estimates, analogous to E-values for unmeasured confounding. Formal proofs (monotonicity + sharpness) for 3 priority topologies; MC-validated conjectures for the remaining 3.

3. **Correction guidance framework**: A principled decision framework mapping {DAG topology × error structure × ASV} to the appropriate correction method (DSL, PPI, MLA, naive plug-in), characterizing regimes where each applies and where no existing method suffices — including dependence-aware multi-LLM correction as an open problem.

## Story Spine

- **Problem**: LLMs are rapidly replacing human annotators in CSS, but Baumann et al. (2025) show 31% of downstream conclusions are already incorrect. Researchers lack diagnostic tools to answer: (a) which annotation error structures propagate bias under their causal design, and (b) how robust their conclusions are to annotation error. Kim et al. (ICML 2025) show cross-model errors are highly correlated (60% agreement when both err), meaning ensembles cannot escape systematic bias — researchers MUST analyze the error structure of their chosen annotator, which is exactly what our tools enable.

- **Existing approaches & gaps**: Wood-Doughty et al. (2018) apply DAG reasoning to text classifier errors but produce no formal bias theorems (binary only). TeBlunthuis et al. (2024) provide the most complete binary treatment with MLA correction but are limited to K=2, single classifier. Lee & Wood-Doughty (2024) extend to categorical + LLM classifiers but cover only 1 DAG topology (unobserved confounding), with no systematic taxonomy or sensitivity analysis. VanderWeele & Li (2019) provide sensitivity bounds but only for binary risk ratios. Jerzak et al. (EMNLP 2025) benchmark correction methods but treat error as monolithic — if different confusion matrix structures produce qualitatively different bias in different DAG topologies, unconditional benchmarking is itself misleading.

- **Our framing**: Multi-class annotation errors are not created equal. The same confusion matrix that produces innocuous residual bias in one DAG topology can produce direction-reversing toxic bias in another. We provide the first systematic characterization of this interaction (the taxonomy), a tool to quantify robustness (ASVs), and guidance for when/how to correct (the framework). This is not a new correction method — it is the missing diagnostic layer that tells researchers which correction is appropriate, or whether correction is needed at all.

- **Headline result template**: "Across 6 DAG topologies with K=3,5,7, our bias expressions correctly predict bias direction and magnitude within 95% MC confidence intervals. On 3 CSS tasks annotated by 3 LLMs, ASVs provide calibrated robustness indicators, and our taxonomy identifies cases where commonly applied corrections would increase rather than decrease bias."

## Core Insight (Lead Finding)

The binary guarantee that "non-differential misclassification biases toward the null" breaks in the multi-class case (Brenner 1993). But Brenner only identifies the danger without resolving the ambiguity. Our taxonomy resolves it: for each {confusion matrix structure × DAG topology} cell, we provide exact conditions determining when bias attenuates, amplifies, or reverses. Furthermore, the natural "fix" of binarizing a K-class variable is itself hazardous — collapsing categories introduces new, direction-unpredictable bias (demonstrated in MVP: Δ up to 0.089 between K=3 and binarized estimates).

## MVP Evidence

Confounding DAG + K=3 validated:
- Theoretical bias expressions match MC perfectly (5/5 structures within 95% CI)
- All non-differential C structures produce positive bias 0.20-0.30 (toward OVB)
- Binary collapse produces different bias (max Δ=0.089)
- 100k random C search: confounding DAG bias is monotonically toward OVB (no direction reversal in this topology)
- Direction reversal expected in mediator/collider topologies — research phase priority

## Venue Fit Risks

- **AAAI**: Broad AI audience — emphasize general methodology for "automated annotation measurement error," not LLM-specific. Frame as extending classical measurement error theory to modern automated labeling.
- **ARR/NAACL**: NLP audience — CSS track is natural fit. May want more empirical NLP experiments. Balance theory with practical LLM annotation scenarios.
- **Cross-discipline bridge**: Epidemiology (measurement error theory) × NLP (annotation errors). Epi reviewers check proof rigor; NLP reviewers check empirical relevance. Must serve both.

## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns & Planned Responses

1. **"Trivial extension of binary to multi-class"** → Brenner (1993) proved direction reversal; our taxonomy provides the first systematic characterization across 6 topologies. Binarizing K-class introduces NEW unpredictable bias (MVP evidence). The complexity jump is structural: binary has 2 free parameters (sensitivity, specificity) → scalar bias; K=5 has 20 free parameters → matrix-valued bias requiring eigendecomposition for interpretation. [Experiments: plan_001, plan_008]

2. **"Lee & Wood-Doughty (2024) already did categorical"** → They cover 1 topology (unobserved confounding) on 1 dataset (MIMIC). We cover 6 topologies with systematic taxonomy + ASVs + correction guidance. Their work is a stepping stone; ours is the full framework. [Experiments: plan_001]

3. **"Why these 6 DAG topologies?"** → These are the canonical CSS causal designs used by Hernán & Cole (2009) and TeBlunthuis et al. (2024). They cover the major roles an annotated variable can play: confounder, mediator, collider, instrument, front-door criterion variable. [Experiments: plan_001]

4. **"K≥5 expressions aren't actionable"** → Three interpretability tools: (a) eigendecomposition summaries identifying dominant bias modes, (b) worst-case scalar bounds, (c) diagnostic visualizations. [Experiments: plan_002]

5. **"ASV sharpness only proved for 3 topologies"** → Honest scoping reflecting algebraic complexity. Remaining 3 validated via MC with numerical sharpness evidence. Full proofs identified as immediate future work. [Experiments: plan_004, plan_005]

6. **"Correlated multi-LLM errors?"** → Kim et al. (ICML 2025) actually STRENGTHENS our case: if ensembles can't fix errors (60% agreement when both err), error structure analysis is the only viable approach. Multi-annotator correction with dependence is identified as an open problem. [Framework discussion]

7. **"Empirical validation scope"** → 3 CSS tasks × 3 LLMs × 3 DAG-relevant scenarios. Tasks selected to cover K=2,3,5 annotation complexity. [Experiments: plan_003, plan_006]
", "total_chars": 7854, "truncated": false}, "error": null, "metadata": {}}

For plan_003, I need to verify that gold-standard labels are available across all the datasets: protest event coding from ACLED/GPT-RE, stance detection from SemEval/VAST, and toxicity from Civil Comments.

SemEval/VAST and Civil Comments have publicly available gold labels, but ACLED's gold labels may have redistribution restrictions under their terms of service, so I should verify data access before proceeding. For the model versions, Llama 4 Maverick from April 2026 is current, and Qwen 3.5 Plus and DeepSeek V4 both seem plausible for 2026 releases given the timeline of their predecessors.

The AAAI abstract deadline is July 21, giving me about two months with ten planned experiments and none started yet. The critical path runs through plan_001 (theory and simulation, likely 2-3 days), then plan_004 (proof work), then plan_006, with plan_003 running in parallel. Plan_001 and plan_004 are dependencies for multiple downstream experiments, so the bottleneck is really plan_004's proof work, which could take longer than the simulation phase.

There's also a data consistency issue in plan_010 where the coverage matrix claim field uses a string instead of integers like the other experiments, which will break the coverage tool. More importantly, the paper framing leads with "binary guarantee breaks" as the core insight, but this hasn't been validated across different topologies yet—the roadmap mentions verifying direction reversal in other topologies, but the current framing doesn't adequately hedge against the scenario where direction reversal turns out to be rare or absent. - P0/P1/P2 分级合理

- API 标注成本估算 $300-550 合理

- [severity: critical] **plan_001 是存在性检验但无 kill criterion**。plan_001 description 说"Key question: which topologies show direction reversal under non-differential error?"——若答案是 0/6 拓扑有反转，paper 核心叙事（"binary guarantee breaks"）需要根本性调整。建议 Director 在 plan_001 完成后设一个 **checkpoint decision**：

content.content:
1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	MVP Validation: Exposure Misclassification DAG — K=3 vs K=2
4	
5	Tests whether the binary "bias toward null" guarantee for non-differential
6	exposure misclassification breaks in the multiclass (K>=3) setting.
7	
8	== Technical Setting ==
9	A is the EXPOSURE/TREATMENT variable, measured with error via LLM annotation.
10	No confounders. Simplest possible misclassification scenario.
11	
12	  DAG: A -> Y, A -> A*
13	  DGP: Y = beta_0 + beta_1*1[A=1] + beta_2*1[A=2] + eps
14	  Misclassification: P(A*=j|A=i) = C[j,i], C column-stochastic
15	
16	Researcher regresses Y ~ 1 + 1[A*=1] + 1[A*=2] instead of Y ~ 1 + 1[A=1] + 1[A=2].
17	
18	== Binary Guarantee (K=2) ==
19	Non-differential misclassification of binary exposure guarantees bias toward
20	null: the estimated effect is attenuated (|gamma_hat| <= |beta|). This is
21	a classical result in measurement error literature.
22	
23	== Key Question ==
24	Does this guarantee extend to K=3? Or can certain confusion matrix structures
25	produce:
26	  - SIGN REVERSAL: sign(gamma_hat_k) != sign(beta_k)
27	  - AMPLIFICATION: |gamma_hat_k| > |beta_k|
28	
29	== Distinction from Lee & Wood-Doughty (2024) ==
30	We study OBSERVED exposure with noisy measurement (A observable, A* used at
31	scale). LWD study UNOBSERVED confounding with proxy (different identifiability).
32	
33	Dependencies: numpy
34	"""
35	
36	import numpy as np
37	from collections import OrderedDict
38	import time
39	
40	
41	# ============================================================
42	# DGP Parameters
43	# ============================================================
44	N_SAMPLES = 10_000
45	M_REPS = 1_000
46	N_RANDOM_SEARCH = 100_000
47	SEED = 42
48	
49	P_A = np.array([0.4, 0.35, 0.25])
50	BETA = np.array([0.0, 1.0, -0.5])    # beta_0, beta_1, beta_2
51	SIGMA_Y = 1.0
52	
53	
54	# ============================================================
55	# Confusion Matrix Structures (reused from confounding DAG MVP)
56	# ============================================================
57	
58	C1_SYMMETRIC_HIGH = np.array([
59	    [0.80, 0.10, 0.10],
60	    [0.10, 0.80, 0.10],
61	    [0.10, 0.10, 0.80],
62	])
63	C1_DESC = "Symmetric high-accuracy: diag=0.8, uniform off-diagonal=0.1"
64	
65	C2_ASYMMETRIC = np.array([
66	    [0.65, 0.05, 0.10],
67	    [0.30, 0.85, 0.10],
68	    [0.05, 0.10, 0.80],
69	])
70	C2_DESC = "Asymmetric: P(A*=1|A=0)=0.30 >> P(A*=0|A=1)=0.05"
71	
72	C3_STRUCTURAL_12 = np.array([
73	    [0.96, 0.01, 0.01],
74	    [0.02, 0.69, 0.30],
75	    [0.02, 0.30, 0.69],
76	])
77	C3_DESC = "Structural: classes 1<->2 heavily confused (0.30), class 0 clean"
78	
79	C4_WEAK_DIAG = np.array([
80	    [0.40, 0.35, 0.25],
81	    [0.35, 0.40, 0.35],
82	    [0.25, 0.25, 0.40],
83	])
84	C4_DESC = "Weak diagonal dominance: diag~0.4, non-uniform off-diagonal"
85	
86	C5_NEAR_PERM = np.array([
87	    [0.05, 0.05, 0.90],
88	    [0.90, 0.05, 0.05],
89	    [0.05, 0.90, 0.05],
90	])
91	C5_DESC = "Near-permutation: cyclic 0->1, 1->2, 2->0 (p=0.90)"
92	
93	C6_DIFF_BASE = np.array([
94	    [0.80, 0.10, 0.10],
95	    [0.10, 0.80, 0.10],
96	    [0.10, 0.10, 0.80],
97	])
98	C6_DESC = "Differential base (=C1 in non-diff exposure setting; Y-dependent in MC)"
99	
100	
101	def make_confusion_matrices():
102	    """6 confusion matrix structures."""
103	    matrices = OrderedDict([
104	        ("1_sym_high",   (C1_SYMMETRIC_HIGH, C1_DESC)),
105	        ("2_asymmetric", (C2_ASYMMETRIC,     C2_DESC)),
106	        ("3_struct_12",  (C3_STRUCTURAL_12,  C3_DESC)),
107	        ("4_weak_diag",  (C4_WEAK_DIAG,      C4_DESC)),
108	        ("5_near_perm",  (C5_NEAR_PERM,      C5_DESC)),
109	        ("6_diff_base",  (C6_DIFF_BASE,      C6_DESC)),
110	    ])
111	    for name, (C, _) in matrices.items():
112	        assert np.allclose(C.sum(axis=0), 1.0), f"{name}: columns don't sum to 1"
113	    return matrices
114	
115	
116	# ============================================================
117	# Theoretical bias (exact)
118	# ============================================================
119	def theoretical_bias_exposure(C, p_A, beta):
120	    """
121	    plim gamma = (E[Z'Z])^{-1} E[Z'X] beta
122	    Z = (1, D*_1, D*_2),  X = (1, D_1, D_2)
123	
124	    Returns: (plim_gamma, bias_vector)
125	    """
126	    p0, p1, p2 = p_A
127	    q = C @ p_A
128	
129	    EZZ = np.array([
130	        [1.0,  q[1], q[2]],
131	        [q[1], q[1], 0.0],
132	        [q[2], 0.0,  q[2]],
133	    ])
134	
135	    EZX = np.array([
136	        [1.0,  p1,            p2],
137	        [q[1], C[1, 1] * p1,  C[1, 2] * p2],
138	        [q[2], C[2, 1] * p1,  C[2, 2] * p2],
139	    ])
140	
141	    plim = np.linalg.solve(EZZ, EZX @ beta)
142	    return plim, plim - beta
143	
144	
145	# ============================================================
146	# Data generation & OLS
147	# ============================================================
148	def _generate_Astar(A, C, rng):
149	    """Vectorized A* sampling from confusion matrix."""
150	    probs = C[:, A]
151	    cum = np.cumsum(probs, axis=0)
152	    u = rng.uniform(size=len(A))
153	    return ((u >= cum[0]).astype(int) + (u >= cum[1]).astype(int))
154	
155	
156	def _generate_Astar_diff_Y(A, Y, C_base, rng, factor=2.0):
157	    """Differential: Y > median => off-diagonal rates scaled by factor."""
158	    C_high = C_base.copy()
159	    for col in range(3):
160	        diag_val = C_high[col, col]
161	        off_sum = 1.0 - diag_val
162	        new_off_sum = min(off_sum * factor, 0.95)
163	        scale = new_off_sum / off_sum if off_sum > 0 else 1.0
164	        for row in range(3):
165	            if row != col:
166	                C_high[row, col] *= scale
167	        C_high[col, col] = 1.0 - sum(C_high[r, col] for r in range(3) if r != col)
168	
169	    Y_med = np.median(Y)
170	    high = Y > Y_med
171	    probs_low = C_base[:, A]
172	    probs_high = C_high[:, A]
173	    probs = np.where(high[np.newaxis, :], probs_high, probs_low)
174	    cum = np.cumsum(probs, axis=0)
175	    u = rng.uniform(size=len(A))
176	    return ((u >= cum[0]).astype(int) + (u >= cum[1]).astype(int))
177	
178	
179	def ols_coefs(X, Y):
180	    """OLS coefficients."""
181	    return np.linalg.lstsq(X, Y, rcond=None)[0]
182	
183	
184	# ============================================================
185	# Monte Carlo
186	# ============================================================
187	def run_mc_exposure(M, N, C, p_A, beta, sigma_Y, seed, differential=False):
188	    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
189	    bias_misclass = np.empty((M, 3))
190	
191	    for m in range(M):
192	        A = rng.choice(3, size=N, p=p_A)
193	        D1 = (A == 1).astype(float)
194	        D2 = (A == 2).astype(float)
195	        Y = beta[0] + beta[1] * D1 + beta[2] * D2 + rng.normal(0, sigma_Y, N)
196	
197	        if differential:
198	            A_star = _generate_Astar_diff_Y(A, Y, C, rng)
199	        else:
200	            A_star = _generate_Astar(A, C, rng)
201	
202	        D1s = (A_star == 1).astype(float)
203	        D2s = (A_star == 2).astype(float)
204	        X_star = np.column_stack([np.ones(N), D1s, D2s])
205	        gamma_hat = ols_coefs(X_star, Y)
206	        bias_misclass[m] = gamma_hat - beta
207	
208	    return bias_misclass
209

213	# ============================================================
214	def binary_attenuation_theory(C_bin, p_bin, beta_bin):
215	    """
216	    Binary exposure misclassification: plim from 2x2 system.
217	    Z = (1, D*), X = (1, D), beta = (beta_0, beta_1)
218	    """
219	    p0, p1 = p_bin
220	    q1 = C_bin[1, 0] * p0 + C_bin[1, 1] * p1
221	
222	    EZZ = np.array([[1.0, q1], [q1, q1]])
223	    EZX = np.array([[1.0, p1], [q1, C_bin[1, 1] * p1]])
224	
225	    plim = np.linalg.solve(EZZ, EZX @ beta_bin)
226	    return plim[1], plim[1] / beta_bin[1] if abs(beta_bin[1]) > 1e-10 else np.nan
227	
228	
229	def collapse_to_binary(C, p_A):
230	    """Derive 2x2 C from 3x3 by collapsing {1,2} -> 1."""
231	    p0, p1, p2 = p_A
232	    pB1 = p1 + p2
233	
234	    c00 = C[0, 0]
235	    c10 = C[1, 0] + C[2, 0]
236	    c01 = (C[0, 1] * p1 + C[0, 2] * p2) / pB1
237	    c11 = 1.0 - c01
238	
239	    C_bin = np.array([[c00, c01], [c10, c11]])
240	    p_bin = np.array([p0, pB1])
241	    beta_bin_eff = (BETA[1] * p1 + BETA[2] * p2) / pB1
242	    beta_bin = np.array([BETA[0], beta_bin_eff])
243	
244	    return C_bin, p_bin, beta_bin

250	def classify_bias(plim_gamma, beta):
251	    """Classify bias type for each component (1 and 2)."""
252	    results = {}
253	    for k in [1, 2]:
254	        g = plim_gamma[k]
255	        b = beta[k]
256	        if abs(b) < 1e-10:
257	            results[k] = "zero_true"
258	            continue
259	        if g * b < 0:
260	            results[k] = "SIGN_REVERSAL"
261	        elif abs(g) > abs(b):
262	            results[k] = "AMPLIFICATION"
263	        else:
264	            results[k] = "toward_null"
265	    return results
